unit_notes.price: BIS Residential Property Prices for BANGKOK, Thailand, NOMINAL, index 2010=100 (FRED mirror id QTHN628BIS; title on FRED is literally "Residential Property Prices for Bangkok, Thailand" -> this is the CITY series, not a nationwide one. Underlying source: BIS selected residential property price series). Quarterly level, no seasonal adjustment. Full coverage 1991Q1-2026Q1, no gaps. Real (CPI-deflated) counterpart is QTHR628BIS if needed. https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/QTHN628BIS
unit_notes.pti: NOT SOURCED. No official Thai price-to-income ratio exists; all null. Valuation must fall back to price/income downstream -- but read the `income` note first, that fallback only has 2014Q1-2025Q4 of denominator.
unit_notes.months: NOT SOURCED -- all null. Thailand has no official public housing supply/inventory series. REIC (reic.or.th) is a JS SPA whose statistics pages cannot be extracted (documented failure in .claude/notes/market-page-spec.md from the /th page round; retried and failed again here). The private surveys that do exist (AREA, SCB EIC, Knight Frank) are annual, cover only c.2021-2026, and disagree on the Greater Bangkok boundary by >60% on the same concept (AREA 210,112 vs SCB EIC 213,000 vs Knight Frank 350,000 unsold units), so they cannot be chained into a quarterly series. Supply axis will be short one component for Thailand.
unit_notes.vacancy: NOT SOURCED -- all null. No Thai equivalent of SQM/REIS rental vacancy exists publicly. See the `months` note: the supply axis has NO components at all for Thailand.
unit_notes.pop: World Bank World Development Indicators, Population, total, Thailand (FRED mirror id POPTOTTHA647NWDB). ANNUAL, mid-year estimate. *** FORWARD-FILLED ONTO THE QUARTERLY AXIS AS A STEP FUNCTION *** -- the same annual value is repeated across all four quarters of its year, so within-year quarter-on-quarter population change is identically zero by construction and only the Q4->Q1 step carries information. Engines with special handling for annual-on-quarterly inputs must apply it here. Coverage 1991-2025; 2026Q1 null (2026 WDI value not yet released). Thailand`s population peaked in 2022 (71,735,329) and has fallen every year since -- that decline is real, not a data artefact. https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/POPTOTTHA647NWDB
unit_notes.credit: BIS Total Credit to Households and NPISHs, Thailand, from ALL SECTORS, *** ADJUSTED FOR BREAKS ***, BILLIONS OF THAI BAHT -- i.e. a LEVEL in domestic currency, market value (FRED mirror id CRDQTHAHABIS). Quarterly, end of quarter, not seasonally adjusted. Coverage 1991Q4-2025Q4; 1991Q1-1991Q3 null (series begins 1991Q4) and 2026Q1 null (BIS credit lags the BIS price series by one quarter). DELIBERATE CHOICE OF ID: the break-UNadjusted twin CRDQTHAHUBIS starts at 255.897bn in 1991Q4 vs 793.563bn for the adjusted series -- a ~3x level break from a coverage expansion -- and would produce enormous fake credit-growth spikes. The adjusted series was verified against the published ratio series QTHHAM770A (credit to households, % of GDP): 793.563bn over 1991 nominal GDP reproduces the published 30.7%, and 16,597.258bn / 87.5% reproduces 2025Q4 nominal GDP of c.18.97trn baht. The USD-denominated twin QTHHAMUSDA was REJECTED because it embeds the THB/USD rate and would show a fake ~50% credit collapse at the 1997 baht float. The 1997Q2-2002Q2 decline in this series (3,047bn -> 2,472bn) is a REAL post-crisis household deleveraging, not a break. https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CRDQTHAHABIS
unit_notes.rate: Bank of Thailand policy rate, per cent per annum, quarterly. SPLICED FROM TWO IMF SERIES: (a) 1991Q1-2000Q2 = IMF MFS_IR THA.MMRT_RT_PT_A_PT.Q, Money Market Rate (interbank overnight); (b) 2000Q3-2026Q1 = IMF MFS_IR THA.MFS166_RT_PT_A_PT.Q, the BOT policy rate (14-day repo from the May-2000 adoption of inflation targeting, 1-day repo from 2007). SPLICE JOIN: 2000Q2 money-market 1.977% -> 2000Q3 policy 1.500%; the ~0.48pp step at the join is a level discontinuity, so the 2000Q3-2001Q2 year-on-year change in this series is not clean. The pre-2000 leg is a market rate, not an administered target, so the 1997-98 spike (1997Q3 19.32% -> 1998Q1 20.64%) is the real crisis money-market squeeze and is correct, but it is a different concept from the post-2000 leg. Verified against known BOT history: 0.50% floor through COVID (2020Q2-2022Q2), hiking cycle from 2022Q3, 2.50% peak 2023Q3-2024Q3, then cuts to 1.00% at 2026Q1. Source: IMF Data (api.imf.org SDMX 2.1), dataflow MFS_IR.
unit_notes.cpi: IMF Consumer Price Index (CPI) dataflow, Thailand, all items (_T), STANDARD REFERENCE PERIOD INDEX: key THA.CPI._T.SRP_IX.Q. Quarterly index level, base 2010=100 (verified: the four 2010 quarters average to 100.000). Source data are Ministry of Commerce CPI. Full coverage on this axis (underlying series runs 1970Q1-2026Q2, truncated here to 1991Q1-2026Q1). CHOICE OF ID: the plain national index THA.CPI._T.IX.Q was REJECTED because IMF only carries it from 2010Q1 and it is re-based over time; SRP_IX is the break-free common-reference-period chain and is the correct deflator. Sanity-checked: the index falls from 122.677 (2025Q1) to 122.018 (2026Q1), matching the well-documented Thai CPI deflation through 2025-26. Source: IMF Data (api.imf.org SDMX 2.1), dataflow CPI.
unit_notes.gdp: IMF Quarterly National Economic Accounts, Thailand, Gross domestic product (B1GQ), CURRENT PRICES (V), SEASONALLY ADJUSTED (SA), domestic currency (XDC): key THA.B1GQ.V.SA.XDC.Q. Underlying source is NESDC national accounts. *** STORED HERE IN BILLIONS OF BAHT PER QUARTER *** (the API returns units of baht; divided by 1e9). This is a quarterly flow, NOT an annualised rate and NOT a 4-quarter sum. Coverage 1993Q1-2026Q1; 1991Q1-1992Q4 null (IMF QNEA for Thailand begins 1993Q1). Sanity-checked against the 1997-98 crisis (1997Q2 1,213bn -> 1998Q2 1,152bn) and the COVID trough (2020Q2 3,640bn). Source: IMF Data (api.imf.org SDMX 2.1), dataflow QNEA.
unit_notes.unemp: IMF Labour Statistics, Thailand, unemployment rate, per cent: key THA.U.PT.Q. Underlying source is the NSO Labour Force Survey. Coverage 2001Q1-2026Q1; pre-2001 null. *** THREE GENUINE HOLES INSIDE THE COVERAGE, LEFT AS NULLS, NOT INTERPOLATED ***: 2020Q2, and the whole run 2021Q1-2022Q3 (7 consecutive quarters) are absent from the source. That means the COVID labour shock is only half observed. Thai unemployment is structurally around 1% because of the large informal/agricultural sector, so its z-score is dominated by very small absolute moves; treat the economy axis accordingly. Source: IMF Data (api.imf.org SDMX 2.1), dataflow LS.
unit_notes.income: *** NOT HOUSEHOLD DISPOSABLE INCOME. *** ILOSTAT, Thailand, Average monthly earnings of EMPLOYEES, both sexes, local currency (BAHT PER MONTH PER EMPLOYEE): indicator EAR_EMTA_SEX_NB_Q, sex=SEX_T, from the NSO Labour Force Survey. This is a per-employee wage level, not a household aggregate and not a national-accounts income measure -- it is NOT unit-comparable to the `income` field in au_raw.json (ABS household gross disposable income, A$m). It is included only because it is the one genuine, observed, quarterly Thai income series that could be obtained. COVERAGE IS ONLY 2014Q1-2025Q4 (48 quarters of a 141-quarter axis); everything before 2014Q1 and 2026Q1 are null. The NSO Household Socio-Economic Survey (the proper household income source) remains unobtainable -- it also failed in the earlier /th page round. *** 2015Q1 IS NULLED ON PURPOSE ***: ILOSTAT publishes 1076.029 for that quarter (and 1094.989 / 1052.500 for the male/female breakdowns), roughly one thirteenth of both neighbouring quarters -- an evident source-side unit error. It was removed rather than interpolated. CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY ENGINE: with pti null and income null before 2014, a price/income valuation reading is impossible for Thailand before 2014Q1, and the 24-quarter standardisation window means the first trustworthy valuation z-score is no earlier than about 2020. Do not report a Thai valuation number outside that window.
